invariant: The thread-local registry belongs exclusively to the dynamic extent of one successful installation. Normal return transfers the collected registry to its caller; unwinding releases it without replacing the initiating panic. A nested installation remains unsupported and must neither replace nor clear the outer registry when its rejection is caught inside the outer body.
causal_divergence: Java holds background filters on each SvgGraphics instance. Rust adapts that per-render ownership to thread-local CURRENT but takes CURRENT only after body returns normally. A sequence panic leaves Some(registry) installed, causing every subsequent same-thread render to fail the reentrancy assertion. A cleanup guard created before checking/installing the registry would introduce a second bug: a rejected nested call could erase the outer render's state.
planned_change: Introduce an RAII scope guard only after successful installation. Its destructor removes CURRENT during both ordinary return and unwind. Keep normal registry transfer and the existing nested-call assertion; do not catch or suppress the body panic. Add same-thread unwind/reuse, successful transfer, and caught/uncaught nested rejection tests, plus ordinary and background-text SVG comparisons against clean renders.
perturbation_axes: Normal return versus body panic versus nested-installation panic, including a nested rejection caught inside an outer render
Ordinary text versus multiple background colors and distinct source seeds on the next same-thread render
verification_plan: Run focused filter registry unit tests against the old code to establish failure, then against the repair
Run full renderer/parser sequence units and all 874 perturbations in-process and isolated per input; initiating renderer failures remain failures

journey_exception: Registry cleanup is an in-process renderer lifecycle property. Unit tests exercise the real parse/render_svg path on the same thread after a caught body panic; separate CLI processes cannot detect leaked thread-local state. Real CLI/Java comparisons remain part of the surrounding sequence packet.
